constitutive_assumptions: Sub-elements and shear connectors exhibit linear-elastic behavior.
Euler-Bernoulli beam theory applies to the sub-elements (shear deformations and rotary inertia are neglected).
Mechanical fasteners are evenly spaced and modeled as providing uniformly distributed slip forces or interlayer shear stresses with a constant slip modulus K.
Axial compressive load is applied at the centroid of the fully composite section, producing uniform axial strain without inducing primary bending moments.
Buckling length coefficients for partially composite columns under the four Euler boundary conditions can be taken as practically identical to those for solid or fully composite columns.
control_variables: Member lengths (L = 6 m for steel-concrete, L = 4 m for timber-concrete).
Sub-element cross-sectional dimensions and material moduli (modulus of elasticity, cross-sectional area, moment of inertia).
Centroidal position of the resultant axial compressive load.
dependent_variables: Internal bending moments of the total cross-section and individual sub-elements.
Internal axial and normal forces in the sub-elements.
Internal shear forces in the sub-elements.
Interlayer slip forces per unit length.
Magnification factors and convenience factors (chi) for deflection, moment, axial force, shear force, and slip force.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The effective bending stiffness of partially composite members can be formulated as a function of the fully composite and non-composite stiffnesses, buckling length coefficient, and the composite action parameter.

Second-order deflections and bending moments in composite beam-columns with interlayer slip can be approximated with high accuracy by applying magnification factors based on critical buckling load to first-order solutions.
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: analytical derivation and case study validation

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Using the deflection magnification factor instead of the shear magnification factor to scale slip forces substantially reduces approximation error and provides conservative estimates.
Moment convenience factors show minimal sensitivity to the degree of interlayer slip, remaining close to values established for solid homogeneous beam-columns.

future_work: Detailed evaluation and validation of exact and approximate convenience factors for beam-columns under other Euler boundary conditions and varied transverse loading configurations.
General application and validation of the approximate analysis method for design practice across practical ranges of geometric and elastic parameters.
independent_variables: Composite action parameter (alpha * L) / shear connector slip modulus (K).
Axial compressive load magnitude and load ratio (P / P_cr).
Transverse loading distribution (uniform distributed load, concentrated load, applied end moments).
limitations_inferred: No direct physical experiments were performed within the study; validation relied solely on comparisons with exact analytical closed-form solutions.
The formulation assumes constant linear slip modulus, neglecting nonlinear connector response, interfacial slip yielding, friction, and connector uplift/separation.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The approximate procedure was evaluated in detail primarily for simply supported beam-columns and requires re-evaluation for other boundary and loading conditions.
Accuracy for shear forces and slip forces deteriorates significantly in members with very flexible shear connectors (very low shear connector stiffness).
In cases with applied end moments, the partial composite action theory gives incorrect values for slip forces at the boundary where the moment is applied.

For large asymmetric loading or asymmetric boundary conditions, a single magnification factor cannot accurately predict second-order deflections at arbitrary locations without deriving position-dependent deflection factors.
main_results: For simply supported partially composite beam-columns, the approximate second-order method agreed closely with exact second-order analysis, yielding maximum errors under 0.2% for deflections, under 0.5% for internal moments, under 1.2% for axial forces, and under 1.4% for shear forces across practical composite action parameters.

Interlayer slip forces predicted via the shear magnification factor exhibited errors up to approximately 9%, but applying the deflection magnification factor reduced this error to about 1.3% while yielding conservative estimates.

For simply supported members with shear connector stiffness of structural significance, adopting the deflection magnification factor across all internal actions offers a simplified and accurate engineering analysis approach.

Approximating first-order deflections and slopes using the proposed effective bending stiffness introduced minimal error (+0.2% for maximum deflection and 0.8% for maximum slope in representative cases).
modeling_methods: First-order and second-order governing differential equations derived from Euler-Bernoulli beam theory for partial composite members with interlayer slip.
Magnification factor approach derived from initial deflected shapes and fundamental buckling loads (eigenvalues).
Effective bending stiffness formulation incorporating buckling length coefficients across Euler cases.
Decomposition of fixed-fixed (Euler case 4) and propped cantilever (Euler case 3) beam-columns at inflection (zero-moment) points into equivalent cantilever and hinged segments.
performance_metrics: Percentage error of approximate second-order deflections and internal actions relative to exact second-order analytical solutions.
Critical buckling load (P_cr) and effective bending stiffness (EI_eff).
possible_gap_implications: The mechanics of partial interaction, interlayer slip, and effective bending stiffness under combined axial compression and bending could provide analytical modeling foundations for multi-layer variable-stiffness structures or continuum robotic mechanisms relying on layer jamming or interface shear.
paper.research_objective: To develop and evaluate a generalized, accurate approximate second-order analysis procedure using magnification factors applied to first-order solutions to estimate deflections and internal actions in composite beam-columns with interlayer slip under Euler boundary conditions.
paper.research_problem: Exact second-order analysis of composite beam-columns with interlayer slip under combined transverse and axial compressive loads is mathematically involved and cumbersome for practical engineering design.
paper.title: Composite beam–columns with interlayer slip—Approximate analysis
